question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 20 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The increase in request volume and error rate are likely due to the flash sale campaign going live.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at 02:35 UTC, causing a surge in request volume.
The surge in requests led to increased load on the system, causing higher latency.
The increased load also resulted in higher error rates due to system strain.

contributing_factors.description: The change in auth feature flag could have contributed to the increase in latency.
why_chain: The auth feature flag was changed to 50% at the same time as the latency spike.
The change in feature flag may have affected the system's performance.
The system may have been underperforming due to the change, leading to increased latency.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment of auth v3.26 could have caused the latency spike.
why_chain: The auth v3.26 deployment happened 200 minutes before the change point.
The deployment could have introduced a bug or incompatibility.
This could have led to increased latency and error rates.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a bug in the autoscaler.
ruled_out.reason: The autoscaler scaling out happened 20 minutes after the change point.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a data issue.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of bad or unusual input data.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region eu-west rose from 137 ms to 246 ms (+80%), with a change point at 2026-03-20T02:35:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region eu-west: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region eu-west rose (2132 per 5 min before, 7230 per 5 min after, +239%).
At the same time, error rate for region eu-west rose (0.39% before, 0.80% after, +105%).
Changed auth feature flag new_ui_flow to 50% in eu-west (auth, eu-west; 2 min before the change; record R011)
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in eu-west at 02:35 UTC (eu-west; 242 min before the change; record R008)
Request volume 3x normal in eu-west (eu-west; 12 min after the change; record R012)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (eu-west; 20 min after the change; record R013)
Deployed auth v3.26 to us-east (routine release) (auth, us-east; 200 min before the change; record R010)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (242 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✗ 1 other change event(s) fit about as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
✗ Two or more changes fit equally well, so the cause cannot be confirmed.
missing_data: Details to tell the competing changes apart (e.g. a rollback test)

actions.action: Roll back the auth feature flag change to 50%.
Review the auth v3.26 deployment for any issues.
Monitor request volume and error rates closely in the future.
